name: wf-step-retrieve
description: Shared retrieval step: one query in, ranked passages out. Embeds the query with bge-m3, then calls nlq.search_knowledge (hybrid, RRF) and logs the hit list to obs.retrievals. Returns one of two shapes depending on the `mode` input — `text` gives the model a single [S1]..[Sn] labelled block, `rows` gives a capability the structured rows with chunk_id. Called by chat-agent's search_brewing_knowledge tool and by cap-brainstorm-pairing steps 2a and 2b.

nodes.name: Normalise input
nodes.notes: The only validation point on the retrieval path. ⛔ `mode` MUST be carried through here: `Return rows` reads it from THIS node, not from the trigger, so dropping it silently forces the text shape and every capability that asked for `rows` gets an empty array. doc_type is fail-open — an unrecognised value becomes '' and NULLIF turns that into a whole-corpus search, so a typo costs scope, not an error. top_k is clamped to 1..8, default 6.

nodes.name: Return rows
nodes.notes: Two output shapes from one node, chosen by `mode`. `rows` returns the structured rows for a capability, where zero results is a valid answer and the caller decides if that is fatal; `text` returns ONE item with ONE `response` key, because the toolWorkflow node hands the model only the last output — this is where the [S1]..[Sn] labels the system prompt cites are actually minted, and the page suffix is null-safe for page-less sources. The chunk_id filter is load-bearing: Always Output Data is ON upstream, so a zero-row search arrives as one empty item rather than none.

parameters.query:
-- The gap CTE is the DRIVING side of the join and always yields exactly one row,
-- so the flag survives even a zero-row search. Not that one is reachable:
-- nlq.search_knowledge's vector arm has no relevance predicate, so it always
-- returns p_limit rows -- which is precisely why "the corpus found nothing" is
-- not an available signal and this function exists instead.
WITH g AS (SELECT * FROM nlq.corpus_vocabulary_gap($1::text))
SELECT s.chunk_id, s.doc_title, s.heading_path, s.page_from, s.raw_content,
       g.gap_terms
FROM g
LEFT JOIN LATERAL nlq.search_knowledge(
  $1::text,
  $2::vector,
  $3::int,
  40,
  50,
  'bge-m3',
  NULLIF($4::text, '')
) s ON true;

-- $6 arrives as a JSON array and is parsed here rather than assembled as a
-- Postgres array literal in the expression: lexemes are arbitrary text, and
-- JSON.stringify already escapes what a bare '{a,b}' literal would not.
SELECT obs.f_log_retrieval($1::text, $2::text, $3::bigint[], $4::int, $5::text,
       ARRAY(SELECT jsonb_array_elements_text($6::jsonb))) AS retrieval_id;

options.queryReplacement: ={{ [$('Normalise input').first().json.session_id, $('Normalise input').first().json.query, '{' + $('Search knowledge').all().map(i => i.json.chunk_id).filter(v => v !== null && v !== undefined).join(',') + '}', $('Normalise input').first().json.top_k, $('Normalise input').first().json.mode, JSON.stringify($('Search knowledge').first().json.gap_terms ?? [])] }}
